content.content:
# ffimap

A deterministic scanner of a Rust crate's `unsafe` surface and raw-pointer usage.

ffimap checks a Cargo workspace through a rustc driver and counts, from the
compiler's own HIR and type information, how the crate's code bypasses safe Rust: its
`unsafe` functions, blocks and calls, the raw pointers its functions take or return
and its structs hold in their fields, the primitives they are cast to and built from,
and more. [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) lists every counter.  

It is meant for Rust crates that interact with FFI libraries (C/C++), and is
integrated with [ffibox](https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox)
for building safe FFI bindings. ffimap is also the safety scan
used by [crustify](https://github.com/crustify-rs/crustify).

- **Deterministic.** The same tree gives the same bytes under a fixed
  scanner.
- **Compiler-precise.** Counts are made after macro expansion, `cfg` selection
  and type resolution, which source-text tools cannot do.
- **Fact-driven.** A counter is a declaration or one expression node, with no
  dataflow and no points-to analysis behind it.

## Requirements

- Python 3.13 or newer.
- `rustup`, for the dated nightly the driver is pinned to
  ([`rust-toolchain.toml`](src/ffimap/driver/rust-toolchain.toml)), with its
  `rustc-dev` and `llvm-tools` components.
- A workspace that builds on that nightly, native dependencies included.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffimap.git
python -m pip install -e ffimap
(cd ffimap/src/ffimap/driver && rustup toolchain install)   # the pinned nightly
```

The driver itself is built on the first scan and rebuilt only when the
toolchain changes.

## Usage

```sh
ffimap path/to/workspace --sys-crates libgit2-sys > scan.json
```

`WORKSPACE` is the directory holding the Cargo workspace or package to scan.
ffimap writes no files: the JSON document goes to stdout, and progress and
errors go to stderr.

## CLI

```text
ffimap WORKSPACE [--ffibox] [--sys-crates CRATE[,CRATE...]]
                 [--seams NAMES] [--regions NAMES] [--barriers NAMES]
                 [--sites COUNTER ...]
ffimap diff BEFORE AFTER
ffimap api extract RUSTDOC_JSON [--dep RUSTDOC_JSON ...] [--plumbing CRATES]
ffimap api diff BEFORE AFTER [--dep RUSTDOC_JSON ...] [--items KEYS] [--raw]
                [--format json|text]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--sites COUNTER ...` | Also report where each named counter's increments are in the source (file, count, lines). Each is a counter's dotted path, such as `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub`. |

# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path. An item whose own name is the anchor's path is left out:
  rustdoc rejects an alias equal to its item's name, and the name already
  answers a search for it.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.

Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.

## 4. Signatures

Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:

- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the
trait's, recorded where the trait is.

## 5. Handles and owners

The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,
`FooArc`, `FooVal` and a policy type such as `FooFree` -- are not always
annotated. An unannotated public struct, enum, union or trait of the crate is
**associated** with C items by rule 1, else by rule 2, and a type alias by rule
3; `via` says which rule tied it:

1. `assoc_type`: a trait impl of the type sets an associated type to an
   anchored type, or a trait impl of an anchored type sets one to it.
   `impl CRefSeam for MailmapRef { type Cell = Mailmap; }` and
   `impl CCell for Mailmap { type Ref<'a> = MailmapRef<'a>; }` both tie
   `MailmapRef` to `st::git_mailmap`.
2. `owner`: the type's impls, or the trait's declaration, hold stand-ins; it is
   associated with their C items. A policy type whose `CDrop::c_drop` wraps
   `fn::git_mailmap_free` goes with that item.

# ffimap

A deterministic scanner of a Rust crate's `unsafe` surface and raw-pointer usage.

ffimap checks a Cargo workspace through a rustc driver and counts, from the
compiler's own HIR and type information, how the crate's code bypasses safe Rust: its
`unsafe` functions, blocks and calls, the raw pointers its functions take or return
and its structs hold in their fields, the primitives they are cast to and built from,
and more. [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) lists every counter.  

It is meant for Rust crates that interact with FFI libraries (C/C++), and is
integrated with [ffibox](https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox)
for building safe FFI bindings. ffimap is also the safety scan
used by [crustify](https://github.com/crustify-rs/crustify).

- **Deterministic.** The same tree gives the same bytes under a fixed
  scanner.
- **Compiler-precise.** Counts are made after macro expansion, `cfg` selection
  and type resolution, which source-text tools cannot do.
- **Fact-driven.** A counter is a declaration or one expression node, with no
  dataflow and no points-to analysis behind it.

## Requirements

- Python 3.13 or newer.
- `rustup`, for the dated nightly the driver is pinned to
  ([`rust-toolchain.toml`](src/ffimap/driver/rust-toolchain.toml)), with its
  `rustc-dev` and `llvm-tools` components.
- A workspace that builds on that nightly, native dependencies included.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffimap.git
python -m pip install -e ffimap
(cd ffimap/src/ffimap/driver && rustup toolchain install)   # the pinned nightly
```

The driver itself is built on the first scan and rebuilt only when the
toolchain changes.

```sh
ffimap path/to/workspace --sys-crates libgit2-sys > scan.json
```

ffimap writes no files: the JSON document goes to stdout, and progress and
errors go to stderr.

- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the
trait's, recorded where the trait is.

## 5. Handles and owners

The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,
`FooArc`, `FooVal` and a policy type such as `FooFree` -- are not always
annotated. An unannotated public struct, enum, union or trait of the crate is
**associated** with C items by rule 1, else by rule 2, and a type alias by rule
3; `via` says which rule tied it:

1. `assoc_type`: a trait impl of the type sets an associated type to an
   anchored type, or a trait impl of an anchored type sets one to it.
   `impl CRefSeam for MailmapRef { type Cell = Mailmap; }` and
   `impl CCell for Mailmap { type Ref<'a> = MailmapRef<'a>; }` both tie
   `MailmapRef` to `st::git_mailmap`.
2. `owner`: the type's impls, or the trait's declaration, hold stand-ins; it is
   associated with their C items. A policy type whose `CDrop::c_drop` wraps
   `fn::git_mailmap_free` goes with that item.

# The packaging gate's procedure, for a crate whose dependencies are unpublished

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A procedure worked out by hand that a skill should state: `testing-gates`' Regressions
section says that a batch that changes the raw bindings packages the safe crate, "built
alone in bundled mode from the C it packages, with no build variant selected", and that
"each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source", but not how. The
direct form fails, and the steps that pass were found by trial.

## Evidence

`wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, which allowlists three functions), on base
`2216b0cd0`, the first packaging gate since the tree's change of 2026-11-13:

1. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo package --offline --allow-dirty` stops before verifying:
   `no matching package named glibc-bindings found` (crates.io index). The packaged
   manifest drops the Git source of `glibc-bindings` and the path of `ffibox`, keeping
   their versions, and the workspace's `[patch]` tables, keyed by those sources, do not
   apply to it.
2. `cargo package --offline --allow-dirty --no-verify --exclude-lockfile` packages (697
   files). Extracted under `crustify/tmp/`, the package's manifest needs an empty
   `[workspace]`, since the worktree's own encloses it, and
   `[patch.crates-io] glibc-bindings = { path = "/target/glibc-crustify" }` and
   `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }`.
3. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo build --offline` there then fails in CMake: PCRE2, then
   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.

`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` (the switch of `src/cli/opt.c`, on
`f68ea8660`), the next packaging gate, followed steps 2 and 3 and failed to compile the
package's `lib`: two copies of ffibox, `0.1.1` by path for the crate and `0.1.0` by Git
(`40621a2`) for `glibc-bindings`, whose manifest takes ffibox by Git. The workspace patches
that Git source too (`[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]`), and step 2's
`[patch.crates-io]` does not stand for it. `opt.rs`'s gateway, which compiles from this switch
on, is the first code of the crate to pass a `glibc_bindings` `FileRef` through the crate's
own ffibox traits (`FileRef::from_ptr`, E0599 four times), so `utf8.c`'s gate could not have
met it. With the workspace's Git patch copied into the package's manifest as well, and the
lockfile the first attempt wrote removed, so that the patch applies, the graph holds one
ffibox and the package builds alone (696 files). Its `lib` tests: 829 pass and 58 fail, the
58 needing `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate. So the script copies every `[patch]`
table of the workspace, the Git sources' as well as crates.io's, and resolves with no
lockfile.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.

## Change

   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.

`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` (the switch of `src/cli/opt.c`, on
`f68ea8660`), the next packaging gate, followed steps 2 and 3 and failed to compile the
package's `lib`: two copies of ffibox, `0.1.1` by path for the crate and `0.1.0` by Git
(`40621a2`) for `glibc-bindings`, whose manifest takes ffibox by Git. The workspace patches
that Git source too (`[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]`), and step 2's
`[patch.crates-io]` does not stand for it. `opt.rs`'s gateway, which compiles from this switch
on, is the first code of the crate to pass a `glibc_bindings` `FileRef` through the crate's
own ffibox traits (`FileRef::from_ptr`, E0599 four times), so `utf8.c`'s gate could not have
met it. With the workspace's Git patch copied into the package's manifest as well, and the
lockfile the first attempt wrote removed, so that the patch applies, the graph holds one
ffibox and the package builds alone (696 files). Its `lib` tests: 829 pass and 58 fail, the
58 needing `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate. So the script copies every `[patch]`
table of the workspace, the Git sources' as well as crates.io's, and resolves with no
lockfile.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.

## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as its
`PROPOSAL.md`. It states:

- the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it cites;
- the goal it serves, by name, and the fitness measure of that goal it expects to move;
- its destination;
- the change, or the patch;
- how it was validated;
- the row the record takes when the change lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes;
- its review's verdict; and
- its status: `open`; `deferred`, with what it waits for; `landed`, with the commit it
  landed as; `declined`, with why; or `superseded`, with the proposal that replaces it.

The campaign keeps an index of its proposals, `crustify/evolution/INDEX.md`, one row per
proposal: its slug, its signal in a line, its status, the runs that met the signal, and the
row of the record it matches, if any. The index has one writer per campaign, so that two
runs never write a row at once. It is written as each batch's proposals land, and holds
every proposal of the campaign before a wave launches.

A signal is filed once while its proposal waits. Before a run files a proposal, it reads the
index, in its worktree, and the record, in Crustify's checkout. Campaigns that share a
component's working branch, as a side campaign does with its parent, read each other's index
too:

- where the index holds its signal in a proposal that is `open` or `deferred`, the run files
  nothing new. When that proposal is in the run's own repository, the run adds its evidence
  to it, as an occurrence; otherwise, the run reports the occurrence in its final message,
  and the index's writer records it;
- otherwise, where its signal meets the recurrence signal of a row of the record, the change
  that landed did not hold: the run files a new proposal that cites the row, as
  [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md)'s Record section describes; and
- otherwise, the run files the proposal.

A lesson is not filed as a proposal: `LESSONS.md` records it. A defect in a tool found
while reviewing is a proposal, not a finding on the reviewed code, and is filed with its
reproducer.

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

done < "$out/bins.txt"

echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

commit 680ac73bf4cc9c6f7002ad150a5f040cde7985fb
Author: Marius Momeu <marius.momeu@berkeley.edu>
Date:   Fri Nov 13 18:45:30 2026 +0000

    utf8.c: port 5 items (wave-229/batch-0/run-1)
    
    glb::utf8proc_utf8class
    fn::utf8_charlen
    fn::git_utf8_iterate
    fn::git_utf8_char_length
    fn::git_utf8_valid_buf_length
    
    The module's whole port, waves 229 to 231 folded into one batch. The
    table is a static built by a const fn from its lead-byte ranges;
    utf8_charlen is the private sequence_len; the three functions are the
    native decode_char(&[u8]) -> Result<(char, usize), InvalidCodePoint>,
    char_count and valid_prefix_len. One C defect is not carried over:
    git_utf8_iterate with str_len 0 reads past its size; the port and its
    export refuse empty bytes.
    
    The crate's first ffi_export gateway, under its first export feature,
    ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c, off: the three git_utf8_* exports in
    ffibox's barrier, each checked against its raw binding at compile time.
    The three functions are allowlisted (wrapper.h gains utf8.h), and their
    pointer findings submitted to the ownership store. Four unit_priv,
    eleven unit_pub (carrying over test_utf8__char_length), three doctests
    and six equiv tests. Proposals: export-signature-check (porting-symbols,
    made as crustify dfd557c on its evolution branch, awaiting review) and
    package-gate-procedure (testing-gates).

### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.
- Rust is line coverage over the 13,226 lines of the crate's 42 files under `src/`, with
  `tests/`, the `-sys` crate and dependencies left out by path. The total covers `99.02`% of
  functions and `97.65`% of regions.
- Doctests, run as a suite of their own: 347, of which 346 pass under the nightly. The
  compile-fail doctest on `CommitBuilder` expects `E0624`, which stable reports and the
  nightly does not; it passes on plain. They reach `11.94`% of C lines and `23.30`% of
  Rust lines, and add no line to the four suites' union.

`crustify/scripts/coverage/` holds the scripts that measured them:
`run.sh "$PWD" libgit2 "$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage"`, then
`report.py crustify/tmp/coverage "C=$PWD/c/src/libgit2:$PWD/c/src/util:$PWD/c/include:$PWD/c/deps,Rust=$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage/tree/src" --c crustify/builds/coverage/libgit2.so.1.9.0`.

The UB suites also run under ASan+UBSan, TSan, Miri and BorrowSanitizer in the agents'
gates. Those runs share one test set and are not counted again.

### `libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c` wave 221 batch 0: `dv_info_t`

The module's one type, wrapped ahead of its `port` batch on the same wave branch, since
`sha1.c`'s C reads its layout from the table `sha1_dvs`. `st::dv_info_t` is `DvInfo`, a
`define_ctype!` layout with `DvInfoRef` and `DvInfoMut`, plain data (six `int`s and 80 words),
`Copy`, `Send` and `Sync`, so that the port's table can be a `static`. `DvInfo::new` is a
`const fn` that refuses (`None`) a recompression step outside `0..80` and a mask bit outside
`0..32`, which `sha1_process` uses unchecked as an index into its saved states and as a
shift, and a mask word other than `0` (`DVMASKSIZE` is 1). It takes any type and `k`/`b`.
The four fields `sha1.c` reads have getters (`dv_type`, `recompression_step`, `mask_bit`,
`message_difference`, the last lending `&'a [u32; 80]`). `copied`, `PartialEq`/`Eq` over
every field, and `Debug` are Rust-only. The symbols (`DVMASKSIZE`, the `DV_*_bit` constants,
`sha1_dvs`, `ubc_check`) are left to the port batch. The raw bindings gain `type dv_info_t`,
and `wrapper.h` gains `hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.h`. The analysis is submitted to the ownership
store as the type's `_comment_user`: it has no pointer field and no lifecycle routine.

Tests: 7 `unit_pub` and 2 `ub_safe`, beside 2 compile-fail cases (the lent difference
outliving its record, a shared handle beside the exclusive one). Their data are `sha1_dvs`'s
first record and its terminator. No equivalence test: C builds no record and has no routine
over the type, and the only C that reads one does so through `sha1_dvs`, the port's symbol,
whose equivalence is that batch's. Plain, ASan+UBSan (the compile-fail cases on the nightly
too), TSan and Miri pass the batch's tests, and BSan passes the reborrow test alone. The
module has no C tests and no dependent module, so those are its regression tests; `fmt
--check` and `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` pass on `plain`. Coverage, from
two runs of `crustify/scripts/coverage/run.sh` over the base snapshot and the tree: the
whole workspace's suites pass on both. `ubc_check.rs` is covered to 100% of its 83 lines, 13
functions and 78 regions, with no branch instrumented. C's coverage moves by noise alone, as
no C changed. `Unit tests` counts `--lib` and `unit_pub` together, as the merged `unit` suite
does.

The safety audit scans (ffimap, `--ffibox --sys-crates crate::sys,pcre2_sys --regions
ffi_import,ffi_export`, the 13 seams, no export feature) of the base snapshot and of the
tree: no safe-boundary site falls in the changeset. `&cell` `+1` is `PartialEq::eq`'s `other:
&Self`, as on `CheckoutPerfdata`. `C by value` `+1` is the `define_ctype!` newtype, and
`raw→std` `+1` the lent difference. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by `code.loc.total` (`+118`)
and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+303`). `ffimap api` (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's private
rustdoc JSON): the 5 items are `new`, and every unattributed module is `kept`. The raw
bindings changed, so the crate was packaged and verified alone in bundled mode (700 files)
with no variant. That took the command `crustify/evolution/package-gate-procedure` now
records: the ffibox Git-source patch, at the manifest's `/crustify-rs/ffibox.libgit2-crustify`,
`--exclude-lockfile`, and the side campaigns' installs on `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`,
`OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`. Usage cells are the assistant's.

content.text:
`dv_info_t` is wrapped, tested and landed on `crustify/waves/wave-221` as one commit, `2492d2a9f` (`ubc_check.c: wrap 1 item (wave-221/batch-0/run-1)`). Nothing is blocked.

**What the binding is**
- **Analysis:** `dv_info_t` is plain data (six `int`s and 80 words), with no pointers and no lifecycle routines. Its only C reader, `sha1_process`, uses two fields unchecked: `1 << maskb` is UB unless `0 <= maskb < 32`, and `states[testt]` is out of bounds unless `0 <= testt < 80`.
- **Type:** `DvInfo`, with the handles `DvInfoRef` and `DvInfoMut`. It is `Copy`, `Send` and `Sync`, so the port batch can build `sha1_dvs` as a `static`.
- **Constructor:** `DvInfo::new` is a `const fn` that returns `None` for a step outside `0..80`, a bit outside `0..32`, or a mask word other than 0. That keeps the values C reads unchecked in range.
- **Getters:** only for the four fields `sha1.c` reads: `dv_type`, `recompression_step`, `mask_bit` and `message_difference` (which lends `&[u32; 80]`). `dvK`, `dvB` and `maski` are set by the constructor only.
- **Rust-only extras:** `copied`, `PartialEq`/`Eq` over every field, and `Debug`.
- **Raw bindings:** `type dv_info_t` is allowlisted and `wrapper.h` includes `ubc_check.h`; the bindings were regenerated. The analysis is recorded in wavefront's ownership store.
- **Left to the port batch:** `DVMASKSIZE`, the `DV_*_bit` constants, `sha1_dvs` and `ubc_check`.

**Tests and gates** (all pass)
- **Tests added:** 7 `unit_pub`, 2 `ub_safe` and 2 compile-fail cases. The first is a lent array outliving its record, the second a shared handle beside the exclusive one.
- **No equivalence test:** C builds no `dv_info_t` record and has no routine over it. The only C reader goes through `sha1_dvs`, which is the port batch's symbol.
- **Runs:** plain; ASan/UBSan (compile-fail cases on nightly too); TSan for `Send`/`Sync`; Miri; BSan on the reborrow test alone. Format and clippy with warnings denied pass, through `end-gates` over the commit.
- **Package:** the crate packages and verifies alone in bundled mode (700 files).
